title: Fully funded scholarships for studying in Germany
description: Which scholarships cover living costs in full, who offers them, when to apply and what a strong application looks like.
html:
Public universities in Germany charge almost no tuition, so a fully funded scholarship here means something specific: a monthly stipend that covers living costs, plus insurance and often travel. The main providers pay around €900 to €1,200 a month, which matches or exceeds the amount the visa requires you to prove. This guide explains who offers these scholarships and how to compete for them.

What fully funded means in Germany

A full scholarship typically includes a monthly stipend, health insurance, a travel allowance and sometimes a study and research grant. Because tuition is not a factor, the stipend is the core benefit. Partial scholarships, which are far more common, pay a smaller monthly amount or a one-off grant and are worth having alongside part-time work.

The main providers

The German Academic Exchange Service is by far the largest funder, with programmes for master's and PhD students across most subjects and specific programmes for certain countries and fields. The political foundations, each linked to a party in parliament, fund students who share their values and are active in society. Religious organisations offer scholarships to members and non-members. The national talent programme supports students already enrolled in Germany. Erasmus+ funds mobility within Europe. Universities themselves offer smaller scholarships, and some large companies fund students in their own field.

Funding from your home country

Pakistan's Higher Education Commission runs scholarships for study abroad, sometimes with a requirement to return afterwards, and bilateral programmes between the HEC and German funders are often less competitive than the global programmes. Check the HEC's website and the website of the German embassy in Islamabad.

By study level

Bachelor's scholarships are rare; most funding starts at master's level. Master's students have the widest choice. PhD candidates are often funded through research positions at universities, which are salaried jobs rather than scholarships and come with a work contract.

When to apply

Deadlines fall a year or more before the start of studies. For a programme starting in October, most scholarship applications close between August and December of the previous year. That means researching scholarships at the same time as researching programmes, not after admission.

What makes a strong application

A clear reason for choosing Germany and this programme, evidence of academic strength, engagement beyond the classroom, and a letter of motivation that reads like you rather than like a template. Referees who know you well beat referees with impressive titles. And apply to several programmes: the odds for any single one are low, and the effort transfers.
